accuracy.why: Unchanged from round 1 in sum. Gained: the fact the English carries and the owner has confirmed is now in the Urdu («ثقافتی ورثے کے گاؤں “ارض الحضارات”»), and the hours are in the source's own 12-hour form («صبح 8 بجے سے رات 10 بجے تک»). Still two points off, for three approximations the proof also lists: «قدرتی خوبی» is neither the English wonder nor the Arabic phenomenon; faq[2].q «کس وجہ سے مشہور ہیں؟» leaves «mild temperature» to the answer; and the chamber («قاعة») is now a «کشادہ جگہ», a spacious place, which says less than hall. Nothing is added anywhere: «دنیا کا سب سے بڑا نخلستان» carries no palm and no natural, warmth stays on «عین سردیوں میں».

nativeness.why: Up one. A second reader who had seen nothing before read the round-1 text and found no error of gender, number or postposition and nothing above minor that is the Urdu's own; of his ten Urdu-side points seven are answered in this round — the clock («صبح 8 بجے سے رات 10 بجے تک»), the verbless answer («خوشگوار ٹھنڈک رہتی ہے»), «چٹانوں میں غار ہیں اور بل کھاتے راستے», «کشادہ جگہ» for «ہال», the area cell, the Good-for row («موزوں … فوٹوگرافی»), «قدرت». Three points off for what stays: four small things on which the two readers split or the source binds («عین سردیوں میں», «چھوتے چھوتے رہ جاتی ہیں», «چھن کر آتی ہے» with nothing to filter through, the kicker «ارضیاتی عجوبہ»), a second sentence that is still plain beside the first, and twelve new edits — among them a coined generic and a one-word label — that no blind reader has seen.

compliance.why: Up one. The head name and the clock form are rulings now, not provisional forms; «ہال» is gone; names are byte-identical to the termbase keys («جبل القارہ» x6, «الاحساء» x4, «ہفوف» x1, «ارض الحضارات» x2 inside “ ” and each time after its generic); the independent proof passed ten of its eleven items on the round-1 text and its one finding is applied; the scan of all 29 strings is clean and the 12-hour, currency, generic and gloss guards pass and are shown to bite. One point off: the twelve edits of this round have been checked by this stage only, the stage checker still encodes superseded rules, and two entries stay pending («ثقافتی ورثے کا گاؤں», a phrase built here and not yet read blind; «فوٹوگرافی», whose gender rests on usage).

fit.why: Up one. The two things this reader could not use are answered: he reads the hours as he says them, and he is told what sells the ticket — a heritage village — in the card and in the answer alike. One point off for what the page still cannot tell him because no source says it, all of it raised again by the second reader as moderate: whether the village is at the mountain and whether he can pay at the gate, the child price, which holidays, why daytime, how one reaches the summit, whether narrow corridors suit the family the card invites.

structure.why: Same 29 leaf paths as round 1, stage 5 and the pack, in the same order; the body is one plain-text paragraph; «{op}» once in det.hoursNotice and not in det.hoursNotice.op; det.openMaps keeps « ↗»; no heading or label carries a stop, a bracket or a question mark; the twelve changes replay exactly from the round-1 fields.

blind_reader_rulings.reason: «فطرت» to «قدرت». Both blind readers found the label abstract and both offered «قدرت»; no ground for rejection applies. It remains a UI string: the ui.ur batch settles it with the other category labels and the header-fit measurement, and now starts from the better candidate.
The three strengths are the source's: «warm in winter» in the summary, «a quiet warmth» in the body, «a mild temperature» in the FAQ. The Urdu follows each («گرم», «ہلکی سی گرمائش», «معتدل»). SD16.

Both faults are in a sentence this stage wrote in round 1, and both are real: the passages had lost their place, and «ان میں» attached to «راستے». Rewritten as one phrase in the rock, «چٹانوں میں غار ہیں اور بل کھاتے راستے۔», so that «ان میں» takes both nouns, which is what the source says. His «ان غاروں میں» is not used: it would take the passages out of what stays cool. The sentence is shorter but still plain; that part of (a) is only half answered.

Kept. Both wordings he offers («کڑاکے کی سردی میں», «سخت سردی میں») put a severity where the source has a time (the depth of winter, «قلب الشتاء») — a claim about how cold Al-Ahsa gets that no source makes — and replace the season word with «cold», loosening the tie of warmth to winter that site rule C16 guards. The phrase itself was the first reader's unprompted proposal («an Urdu writer says عین سردیوں میں») and stage 2 called it natural spoken Urdu; «عین» before a period is attested («عین جوانی میں» 6 pages, «عین شباب» 7, «عین موسم سرما» once), though this exact phrase is not (0). Two readers, two ears: carried to the first batch as a point to watch (P18).
Refuge from what is unsaid in both sources («to shelter here», «يأوون إليها»); naming the weather would add. Raised by both readers. SD8.

Kept, and no wording was asked for. The first reader singled this clause out as fully Urdu; the second re-read it and then found it «a pleasing image». The meaning he was unsure of on first pass — the rock stops just short — is exactly the Arabic («يكاد يلمس كتفيك»), and the plainer way to say it is the «تقریباً چھو لیتی ہیں» that stage 4 removed as the English adverb carried over.

«ہال» to «کشادہ جگہ». Two readers, two words («ایوان», then «ہال»), the same built hall in the mind's eye; the first reader's other option is taken in its unambiguous form. Second point, «چھن کر آتی ہے» with nothing to filter through: kept. Both readers noticed it and the first kept the verb in his own rewrite; it is the Arabic's verb («يتسرّب إليها»), and neither source says where the light enters, so the opening cannot be named (the Russian line's «сверху» was removed for the same reason).

The leap from the chamber to the summit, and whether a visitor can go up, by what way and on which ticket: the English body does not say, and the sentence that told him the secret is not in the height is the source's too. Both readers, both moderate. SD1.

«why Al-Ahsa became» is what both sources say. Both readers offered the same softening («کیوں کہا جاتا ہے», «کیوں کہلاتا ہے») and it is declined again: it would turn a claim the Arabic states flatly into a reported one. The remedy belongs in the source. SD2.

What he grades — what Hofuf is and how far — is not in the source (SD10), nor is the double use of Al-Ahsa as region and as oasis the Urdu's (it is in the English and the Arabic alike). The wording point (a) is the Urdu's and is applied: «الاحساء، ہفوف کے مشرق میں», an area name first and one «میں» instead of two (change 2).

«During the daytime.» is all the source has; the reason and the season he asks for cannot be supplied. Both readers, the first high, the second moderate. The final «۔» is noticed by both: it stays because this field is a sentence on other pages and carries a stop in all five languages; if it goes, it goes in the data for every language. SD3.
Owner decision P13: «روزانہ صبح 8 بجے سے رات 10 بجے تک», his own wording, in the card and in the answer (changes 3 and 8). No dash between clock times remains anywhere.

Which holidays and until when: «on holidays», «may be extended». SD4. His side point, that the verb has no subject in sight in the card: kept — the understood subject is the page's own (masculine singular, as in the first question), an ordinary ellipsis in a card cell, and the segment is shared with the answer.
The source gives the adult price only. Both readers. SD5.

Owner decision P15: the name now stands with its generic in both places, «ثقافتی ورثے کے گاؤں “ارض الحضارات”» (changes 4 and 9), the comma between price and ticket line becomes «؛» (change 4), and the bracket that translated the name without saying what it was is dropped (change 5). What stays open is not the Urdu's: no language says whether the village is at the mountain or whether one can pay at the gate, nor whether «the operator» of the notice line is the same body (SD6, SD14).

The label becomes «موزوں» (change 6): the second reader stopped where the first did, which is the test round 1 set. «تصویر کشی» becomes «فوٹوگرافی» (change 7): two independent readers, a headword in Urdu Lughat and the reader's paper's own tag; round 1 is reversed for this word on that evidence. That the row is a mixed bag is the source's (SD9).

How much walking, how tight, how long, and whether it suits the elderly or small children: nothing in the source, which says families and says narrow in the same breath. Stage 3 had been tempted to supply it and rightly did not. SD13.

The sentence is praised; the vagueness is the template's. In every language the linked word says only «the operator» and the link goes to whatever account the data holds; the string cannot name a channel it does not know. SD14, carried to the ui.ur batch.
A seam left by this stage's round-1 change 16, found independently by the proof. The clause after «تو» gets its verb: «خوشگوار ٹھنڈک رہتی ہے» (change 10).
The four answers restate the card and the body in the English and the Arabic too; the things the card leaves open are not in any source. SD15.

Kept, on the same ground as in round 1 and against two readers now: «قدرت کا عجوبہ» says wonder of nature where the kicker's only source says «أعجوبة جيولوجية», and zh, de and ru keep geological. The register cost is real and is recorded (P24) with the one-line option the owner may take; it is not the translation's to take.

proof_rulings.reason: Accepted as stated and corrected with the proof's own two words, «رہتی ہے». The fault was this stage's: round-1 change 16 moved a clause from the body into the answer and left its verb behind, and neither round-1 script could see it. The second blind reader found the same seam on his own (observation 19).

The reframed question stays, and the note's facts are accepted: this is the one place where the Urdu repairs a source defect instead of only logging it. Weighed as asked. Against keeping: the question differs from the English and Arabic ones, and the pair is published alone as FAQPage JSON-LD. For keeping: each language's page emits its own question and answer from its own visible text, so nothing in the structured data requires the questions to match, and the Russian page already differs in the same way; a pair that is published alone has to make sense alone, and the literal pair does not (the first reader: the answer only repeats the fact contained in the question); the repair adds no fact and drops none from the pair; and the second blind reader, who saw only the reframed question, listed all four questions among what reads well. The line between this and SD1–SD5, which were logged and left, is stated as a rule (P23): those can only be repaired by adding a fact. The defect is logged all the same (SD7) and the literal fallback is in the notes for the owner.

The oasis stays named. The proof confirms it is no new fact (the body's last sentence, the area line, answer_en) and that grammar and name form are right. Its one consequence, a fourth token of the head name while P2 was pending, has lapsed: the owner has ruled «الاحساء». The second reader's remark that Al-Ahsa first has an oasis and then is one is the source's double use (SD10), not this edit's.

«قدرتی خوبی» stays, and the note is right that it is the one content word whose meaning the edits moved; it is charged under accuracy in both rounds. The sources themselves disagree (wonder, phenomenon); the Arabic-led «قدرتی مظہر» is what the first reader heard as a textbook, and the second reader read «قدرتی خوبی» and remarked only on «پناہ». Ruled under P19.

fields.title: جبل القارہ
fields.summary: نخلستان کے قلب میں وقت کے تراشے ہوئے غار، جو گرمیوں میں ٹھنڈے رہتے ہیں اور سردیوں میں گرم۔
fields.body: الاحساء کے نخلستان کے بیچوں بیچ جبل القارہ کسی قدیم نگہبان کی طرح سر اٹھائے کھڑا ہے، مگر اس کا راز بلندی میں نہیں، اس کے اندر چھپا ہے۔ چٹانوں میں غار ہیں اور بل کھاتے راستے۔ جب گرمی عروج پر ہو تو ان میں خوشگوار ٹھنڈک رہتی ہے، اور عین سردیوں میں ہلکی سی گرمائش۔ اسی قدرتی خوبی کی وجہ سے الاحساء کے لوگ قدیم زمانے سے یہاں پناہ لیتے آئے ہیں۔ پہاڑ کی تنگ راہداریوں سے گزریں تو چٹانیں کندھوں کو چھوتے چھوتے رہ جاتی ہیں، پھر اچانک راستہ اونچی چھت والی کشادہ جگہ میں جا نکلتا ہے، جہاں روشنی کی ایک باریک کرن چھن کر آتی ہے۔ چوٹی سے نخلستان یوں پھیلا دکھائی دیتا ہے جیسے کھجور کے درختوں کا سمندر ہو۔ یہی ایک منظر بتا دیتا ہے کہ الاحساء دنیا کا سب سے بڑا نخلستان کیوں بنا۔

changes.why: Round-2 reader, observation 3, on a sentence this stage wrote in round 1. Two faults of that edit: «راستے بل کھاتے چلے گئے ہیں» had lost its place (he could not tell whether the passages are in the rock or on the hillside), and with the two nouns in separate clauses «ان میں» of the next sentence attached to the nearer one, «راستے». Caves and passages are one phrase again, both in the rock, with the winding kept on the passages as the first reader asked: «غار ہیں اور بل کھاتے راستے» (the pattern of «ایک میز تھی اور دو کرسیاں»). «ان میں» now takes both, which is what the source says (caves and passages keep the coolness); his own «ان غاروں میں» was not used because it would take the passages out of that. «غار ہیں» still shows the plural (P12).

changes.after: اونچی چھت والی کشادہ جگہ میں
changes.why: Round-2 reader, observation 7: «ہال» made him picture a function room (شادی ہال). The first reader had objected to «ایوان» for the same reason (a palace hall, a parliament) and offered «ہال» or «کھلی جگہ»; two readers, two words for a built hall, the same picture. The first reader's other option is taken, with «کشادہ» for «کھلی»: «راستہ … کھلی جگہ میں جا نکلتا ہے» is also how Urdu says that a path comes out into the open air, while «کشادہ» is the plain opposite of the «تنگ» of the corridors and is what the source's «opens onto» says.
